# Sirach Chapter 5 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)

**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Codex Vaticanus, Sirach 5 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-DC/SIR_005_page_001.jpg

---

1 Don't build your life on what you own. Don't tell yourself, "I have plenty — I'm fine."

2 Don't let your impulses and your own desires call the shots.

3 Don't swagger around saying, "Who's going to stop me?" — the Lord will hold you accountable, make no mistake.

4 Don't assume that because nothing happened after you sinned, it doesn't matter. The Lord is patient — but patient is not the same as blind.

5 Don't presume on forgiveness and use it as a license to keep sinning.

6 Don't tell yourself, "God is merciful — he'll forgive everything I do." Yes, he is merciful — but he is also capable of wrath. And his anger lands on those who make a habit of sin.

7 Don't put off turning back to the Lord. Don't say, "I'll do it tomorrow, and the day after." His anger can erupt without warning, and when the day of reckoning comes, you will be swept away.

8 Don't stake everything on wealth you got by dishonest means. On the day disaster strikes, it will do nothing for you.

9 Don't shift with every wind. Don't travel every road at once. That is the way of people who say one thing and mean another.

10 Know what you believe and stick to it. Mean what you say.

11 Listen fast. Answer slow. If you have something worth saying, say it — if you don't, keep your mouth shut.

12 The same tongue that wins you honor can ruin you. Praise and disgrace both flow from what people say.

13 Don't get a reputation as a gossip. Don't lay traps with your words. Thieves live in shame, and people who talk out of both sides of their mouth will face serious consequences.

14 Don't do wrong — big or small. Don't turn friends into enemies.

15 Don't wreck your reputation — a bad name is nothing but a burden. And don't let your own tongue destroy you.
